$comment: The commits build.py makes, as a base and the features forked from it. Format: a JSON object with 'base' and 'features'. 'base' is the root commit: 'branch' (the base branch, main), 'source' (the directory next to build.py whose files form the commit's tree), 'author' ('name' and 'email', also the committer), 'date' (ISO 8601 with offset) and 'message'. Each entry of 'features' is one feature: 'id', 'title', 'owner' (an id from penguin/owners.json), 'role' ('originating' for the feature whose change the others must absorb, 'running' for a feature already under way), 'fork' (the branch that holds the feature, forked from the base branch), 'area' (the 'scopes', 'paths' and 'contracts' the feature declares when it opens; a contract is one main's penguin/scopes.json declares, so a contract the feature adds is declared in its fork's penguin/scopes.json, not here), 'author' and 'commits'. Each commit lays the files of its 'source' directory over the fork's tree; 'tag' names a lightweight tag on the commit. 'fix' marks a commit of the originating feature that fixes code on main in another scope: its 'scope' is the scope the commit changes, which the merge plan's part for that scope names. The first commit of a feature starts from the base branch, each later one from the fork's previous commit.

base.message:
Base: identity map, analytics models and messaging

Three scopes owned by priya, jun and sam, declared in penguin/scopes.json with their
contracts. penguin/invariants.json declares the analytics and messaging invariants and
their recorded examples.

commits.message:
Add person_id with merge rules

Link identities on login events and on a shared verified email. A merged profile
keeps the latest value of each attribute.

Keep published days' active users on main

daily_active_users counts people by person_id from the first day the identity map
links an event to another identity. Earlier days count identities, so a later
login never changes a published day.

Honour an unsubscribe on any linked identity on main

is_subscribed reads each linked identity's latest consent, so an unsubscribe holds
after a later signup on another identity subscribes the address by default.

Limit the identities a login links to one device

A login links its device to its user while the device has linked fewer than five
users.

Lower the identities per device to one

A limit of five still joins the tablet's users. Each device now links only its
first user.

Add the retention dashboard

Daily active users and day-N retention by first-active-day cohort. Declares
retention_dashboard as an analytics contract.

Add a cutover marker for past metrics

Days before the first day that person_id links an event to another identity count
identities, so a later login never changes them.

Add the re-engagement email audience

Subscribed people inactive since a cutoff day, with unsubscribed addresses
suppressed. Declares reengagement_audience as a messaging contract with recorded
examples.

Honour an unsubscribe from any identity linked to the person

The audience leaves out a person when any linked identity's latest consent is an
unsubscribe.
